name: Niẓām al-Dīn ibn Quṭb al-Dīn al-Anṣārī al-Sihālawī
summary: Teacher of Farangī Maḥall in Lucknow after whom the Dars-i Niẓāmī, the course of the Indian madrasas, is named; in it ṣarf and naḥw run from Mīzān al-ṣarf and Naḥw-i Mīr to al-Shāfiya and Sharḥ Jāmī.
bio: Mullā Niẓām al-Dīn was the son of Quṭb al-Dīn Sihālawī, a scholar killed in 1103/1692, after which the Mughal emperor Awrangzīb gave the family a house in Lucknow, the Farangī Maḥall. There Niẓām al-Dīn taught and fixed the order of books that bears his name.

In the Dars-i Niẓāmī the Arabic sciences come first and are read in Persian at the start: in ṣarf the Mīzān al-ṣarf and the other Persian primers, then al-Shāfiya; in naḥw Naḥw-i Mīr and al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa, then Hidāyat al-naḥw, al-Kāfiya and Sharḥ Jāmī. It is the course our Indian path follows. He died in Lucknow in 1161/1748.
uncertain: His death is given as 1161/1748 or 1153/1740.
